resolutions.researcher_notes: Original current_ref (pipeline-journal.net) RE-VERIFIED live (HTTP 200, content present) - the DEAD_LINK was transient. It describes the EPSCC contract as awarded to CPECC/China Petroleum Pipeline Engineering but 'still in the pre-contract phase, with the final contract terms subject to confirmation' - i.e. awarded, not yet under construction, consistent with GEM Status 'proposed'. Corroborated independently by CRU/BC Insight (contract award to CPECC for the Ar-Ratawi Gas Midstream Project) and Goalfore/MEED (Iraq Council of Ministers approved the tender award 2025-04-03). Three independent sources, all pre-construction/award framing. Tier high.

ConstructionYear 2025 corroborated indirectly: the EPSCC contract was awarded/approved in 2025 (Council of Ministers approval 2025-04-03; contract-win reported June 2025) with a 36-month (three-year) implementation period, and BC Insight notes an interim project reducing flaring 'from the end of 2025'. No source states verbatim 'construction began in 2025', so this is inferred from the 2025 award year + start of the 36-month execution window - hence tier medium rather than high. Three independent sources agree the project entered execution in 2025.

Original current_ref (pipeline-journal.net) RE-VERIFIED live - DEAD_LINK was transient. It gives a 36-month implementation from the mid-2025 award, placing start-up in the 2027-2028 window, consistent with GEM's phased StartYear3=2027. VALUE DISAGREEMENT TO FLAG: BC Insight (CRU) explicitly reports the main Ar-Ratawi Gas Midstream Project commissioning is 'scheduled in 2028', not 2027; earlier partial phasing (flaring reduction from end-2025) makes a 2027 phased start plausible but no source states 2027 verbatim. Kept pipeline-journal as the ref (corroborates the ~3-year build/start-up window); BC Insight listed in verifications with contains_value=false because it points to 2028. Tier medium given the 2027-vs-2028 discrepancy.

Original current_ref (iraq-businessnews.com) is dead (HTTP 401). A Wayback copy re-verifies live but mentions TotalEnergies, NOT the Iraq Ministry of Oil (no 'Ministry' or 'Basra' token on the page), so it does NOT corroborate the GEM Owner value. VALUE DISAGREEMENT TO FLAG: GEM lists Owner1 = 'Iraq Ministry of Oil' 100%, but every independent source describes the project as part of the TotalEnergies-led Gas Growth Integrated Project (GGIP) consortium - TotalEnergies 45% (operator), Basrah Oil Company 30% (state-owned, the Ministry of Oil's operating arm), QatarEnergy 25%; the EPSCC/pipeline contract was awarded via state-owned Basrah Oil Company. No source corroborates '100% Iraq Ministry of Oil'. Basrah Oil Company being an arm of the Ministry of Oil makes majority Iraqi state ownership defensible, but the exact 100%-Ministry attribution is unsupported and partially contradicted by the 45/30/25 consortium split. Left proposed_refs empty (no source corroborates the stated value); recommend Update review the owner field against the GGIP consortium structure. Tier low.
